ai.description: This lizard reaches 25 cm in total length. It is olive-brown with dark dorsal crossbands and a prominent, serrated nuchal crest. A distinct pale stripe runs along the side of the body.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Japalura andersoniana* is distinguished by a prominent, continuous row of enlarged, spine-like scales along the nape and back, which are notably larger than in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Japalura andersoniana* inhabits the humid subtropical forests and temperate broadleaf woodlands of the Eastern Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Anderson's Mountain lizard is primarily diurnal, often observed basking on rocks or tree trunks to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Japalura andersoniana* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from May to August in Northeast India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Japalura andersoniana* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically within Arunachal Pradesh, India, at elevations ranging from approximately 1,500 to 2,500 meters.
